why.text: Most vines grow on poor, light, well-drained soils; on the alluvial plain they give light, silky, fresh wines. Old-vine Garnacha is the classic liqueur wine.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds, and rancio; also needle and sparkling wines; liqueur wines (Garnacha, Moscatel, white and black mistela, vino dulce and rancio); and wines from overripe grapes.

climate.text: Mediterranean, about 600 mm of rain and a mean of 14 to 16 °C a year. The strong, dry north wind, the Tramuntana, keeps the vines healthy.

soil.text: Mostly poor, light, well-drained, acid to neutral soils. In the hills: granite, slate and schist, or gravel, sand and clay; on the alluvial plain: marls and clays, or conglomerates and sandstones.

tastes.text: Reds: violet-red to brick with age; ripe fruit, balsam, spice; smooth, structured, tannic. Whites: pale yellow; fresh, fruity. Rosés: soft pink to cherry; floral, fruity.

styles.name: Mistela
styles.text: White: pale to gold, floral, fruity. Black: red-violet, red fruit. Sweet, balanced.

styles.name: Garnacha
styles.text: Ripe or raisined fruit; Ámbar from white or red grapes, Rubí from Garnacha Tinta.

styles.name: Moscatel
styles.text: At least 90% overripe Muscat of Alexandria or Muscat Blanc; sweet, velvety, intense and long.

styles.name: Uvas sobremaduradas
styles.text: Overripe grapes, 18% natural alcohol; yellow to amber; dried fruit, long.

why.text: Seasonal and day-night swings of up to 25 °C, strongest at ripening, give aromatic, structured wines; cold nights give high acidity and intense flavours.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds; also needle wines, sparkling wines, liqueur wines, and wines from overripe or raisined grapes.

climate.text: Dry continental climate with a wide temperature range, both seasonal and between day and night.

soil.text: Calcareous soils covered with sand and/or clay, poor in organic matter.

tastes.text: Cold nights during ripening give wines of high acidity and intense flavours.

styles.name: Espumoso
styles.text: First or second fermentation, at least 3 bar; a traditional-method history from the early 1900s.

styles.name: Vino de licor
styles.text: White, rosado or red; spirit added to reach 15 to 22% vol.

styles.name: Vino de aguja
styles.text: Visible carbon dioxide at 1 to 2.5 bar; fruit or floral aromas.

why.text: A climate between Mediterranean and continental gives light wines with a good acid core; Pyrenean influence freshens white aromas. Herbs add rosemary, lavender and thyme.

styles.text: Whites (also skin-fermented brisado), rosados and reds; also needle wines, sparkling wines, liqueur wines (rancio, mistela, vino dulce natural) and naturally sweet wines.

climate.text: Temperature and rainfall differ markedly from neighbouring areas, and the average altitude favours the wines. Distance from the sea and the pre-coastal range put the climate midway between Mediterranean and inland continental, which gives light wines with a good acid core.

soil.text: Sedimentary sandstones, mudstones, limestones and conglomerates. On the Pla de Bages, moderately to very deep, medium-textured, well-drained soils; carbonate content is generally high.

tastes.text: Whites: pale to deep gold yellow; fruity; usually light. Rosés: pale pink or onion-skin to cherry red; fruity; usually light. Reds: violet to ochre; fruity; from light and fresh to more structured and concentrated.

styles.name: Espumoso
styles.text: Fruity, sometimes ageing aromas; fresh from the carbon dioxide, which adds structure and breadth.

styles.name: Vino de aguja
styles.text: Fruity aromas; fresh from the carbon dioxide, which adds structure and breadth.

styles.name: Vino de licor
styles.text: Yellow, amber, gold, red or tawny; fresh or ripe fruit aromas; unctuous, long.

why.text: Well-drained granite soil with marine remains makes the vines root deep. The mild stress helps regulate yield.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds; also liqueur wines (rancio, mistela, natural sweet), traditional-method sparkling and needle wines.

climate.text: Mediterranean. On the coast, 550 to 800 mm of rain, mild winters and hot summers; the Coastal Range shelters the vines from cold inland winds and holds the summer sea breeze.

soil.text: Granite subsoil with marine remains, breaking into small grains at the surface; permeable.

tastes.text: Whites, mostly Pansa Blanca: fruity with fresh mineral notes and a bitter, citrus, green-almond finish; baked apple when oaked. Reds, mostly Garnacha Tinta: elegant, broad, long, fruity and mineral. Inland wines show more acidity.

styles.name: Rancio
styles.text: From white Garnacha and Macabeo or red Garnacha; sun-and-night, at least a year in oak.

styles.name: Mistela
styles.text: White-grape free-run must; the wine is filtered at 12% natural alcohol or more, then wine spirit added.

styles.name: Espumoso
styles.text: Traditional method, second fermentation in bottle, nine months before disgorging.

why.text: Trepat, native to Conca de Barberà and nearly exclusive to it, gives rosados, reds and pink sparkling and needle wines of their own character.

styles.text: Whites (also skin-macerated brisado), rosados and reds; also liqueur wines, sparkling wines and needle wines.

climate.text: Transitional Mediterranean, between the mild coast and the continental inland; marked day-night swings, cold winters and summers not too hot. 450 to 550 mm of rain, mean 13 to 14 °C.

soil.text: Three kinds: clay-limestone soils of clay, marl and calcareous conglomerate, poor in organic matter, in the centre; pebbly river terraces; and slate soils with abundant «licorella» in the southeast.

tastes.text: Whites: pale green-yellow to deep gold; fruity and/or floral when young; light, fresh when young. Rosés: bright red-violet to onion-skin; floral, fruity. Reds: intense cherry to ruby; fruity when young, tertiary and even toasty notes after oak.

styles.name: Vino de licor
styles.text: Up to amber with copper glints; rancio dry and intense, dulce natural and mistela unctuous.

styles.name: Espumoso
styles.text: Fresh fruit aromas; fresh, creamy, balanced.

styles.name: Vino de aguja
styles.text: White, rosado or red with carbon dioxide; fruity, floral, fresh, slight tickle.

why.text: Long, hot, sunny summers ripen even late grapes well; cellars at about 13 to 15 °C suit the second fermentation in bottle.

styles.text: Sparkling white and rosé, made by a second fermentation in the bottle.

climate.text: Transitional Mediterranean, between the mild coast and harsher inland. About 500 mm of rain a year and about 2,500 hours of sun.

soil.text: Mostly chalky and fairly clayey, with little sand. Low in organic matter and not very fertile.

tastes.text: White: pale yellow to straw. Rosé: shades of pink. Small, steady bubbles. Fruity, fresh, clean aromas with a note of lees; fresh and balanced, with a yeast note. Gran Reserva: ripe fruit, nuts, toast.

styles.name: Gran Reserva
styles.text: Long contact with yeast; ripe fruit, nuts and toast; complex, clean aromas.

styles.name: Paraje Calificado
styles.text: Complex aromas of nuts and toast; balanced structure, creaminess and acidity.

why.text: Soil, climate and human work come together here to bring white grapes to their best ripeness. The whites get freshness, acidity and fruit.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds, some sweet by the cold-stop «dulce de frío» method; also sparkling, needle and liqueur wines (vino dulce natural, Vino dulce de Malvasía de Sitges), and sweet wines from overripe grapes.

climate.text: A wide temperature gap between day and night in July and August helps red grapes ripen.

soil.text: Active lime 5 to 10%; rooting depth 40 to 120 cm or more, mostly 80 to 120 cm; generally well drained; loam and silt-loam texture.

tastes.text: Whites: pale to dark yellow; white and tropical fruit, ripe fruit if oaked. Rosés: pale pink to cherry; red fruit, slightly acid, soft, fresh. Reds: garnet when young, tawny when aged.

styles.name: Espumoso
styles.text: Traditional or ancestral method; at least fifteen months from tirage to disgorging.

styles.name: Vino de aguja
styles.text: Second fermentation; carbon dioxide pressure between 1 and 2.5 bar.

styles.name: Vino dulce natural
styles.text: Liqueur wine from overripe grapes of at least 240 g/l sugar, spirit added; candied fruit.

styles.name: Dulce de uvas sobremaduradas
styles.text: Made from overripe grapes, no artificial boost to strength.

why.text: Strong sunshine favours deep colours in the wines, especially the reds.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds; lightly sparkling aguja wines; liqueur wines.

climate.text: Mediterranean, with over 2,500 hours of sun a year, mild dry winters and summers not too hot; 350 to over 600 mm of rain, mean 14 to 15 °C. The strong sunshine favours deep colours in the wines.

soil.text: Mostly Miocene sedimentary soils, calcareous and poor in organic matter; Quaternary alluvium near the rivers. Silt and clay dominate the texture.

tastes.text: White: pale greenish to deep gold; fruity or floral, with vanilla and toast if oaked. Rosé: bright red to onion-skin. Red: cherry to pale ruby; young ones light, oaked ones rounder.

styles.name: Vino de aguja
styles.text: Lightly sparkling: a tingle from carbon dioxide; balanced and fresh.

styles.name: Vino de licor
styles.text: Warm, unctuous and long; fruity if unoaked; nutty notes with ageing; colour up to amber.

why.text: Steep slopes have shallow slate soils with bedrock near the surface. The wines are high in dry extract and deep red in colour.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds, including single-estate «vino de finca»; liqueur wines: rancio (no added spirit), vino de licor dulce, white and red mistela, and natural sweet; and wines from overripe grapes, among them Vimblanc.

climate.text: Sheltered from the sea and, by the Montsant range, from cold north winds; marked day-night swings, cold winters and dry, hot summers; mean 14 to 15 °C, 400 to 500 mm of rain; northwest winds blow.

soil.text: Very steep, shallow soils from slate, low in organic matter, with bedrock close to the surface.

tastes.text: Reds: fruity, floral or mineral aromas; balanced, structured, fresh; oak-aged ones show primary, secondary and tertiary aromas. Whites: fruity, floral or milky; fresh, soft. Rosés: fruity, floral.

why.text: Camp de Tarragona, near the sea, gives soft, balanced whites and firm reds. Ribera d'Ebre reds join Cariñena's body and colour with Garnacha's richness.

styles.text: Whites (also skin-macerated brisado), rosados and reds; also sparkling and needle wines; liqueur wines (mistela, moscatel, Garnacha, rancio, Clásico, Vino de Misa); and Vimblanc, a sweet wine from raisined grapes with no added spirit.

climate.text: Direct sea influence in Camp de Tarragona; a continental influence in Ribera d'Ebre.

soil.text: Low-fertility soils; in Camp de Tarragona clays with a chalky crust, in Ribera d'Ebre calcareous clays, marls, limestones, sandstones and conglomerates. Slightly basic (pH 7.1 to 8.6), low in organic matter, mostly loam.

tastes.text: Clean, bright wines. Whites: greenish yellow to gold; fruity, lightly acidic. Rosés: pale pink to cherry; fresh, light. Reds: violet to tawny red. Sparkling: fruity, lightly acidic. Rancio: amber to tawny; nuts, toast, spice; dry.

styles.name: Rancio
styles.text: Amber, red or tawny, old gold as its typical colour; nuts, toast, spice; dry.

styles.name: Mistela, Vimblanc, Moscatel
styles.text: Yellow from white grapes, black-brown from red; alcohol well integrated; Vimblanc lightly sweet.

why.text: Mountains partly shelter the vines from the sea, giving marked day-night swings at ripening. Garnacha, Cariñena and rugged ground give body; old vines give depth.

styles.text: Mainly reds, with whites (also skin-fermented brisado) and rosados; liqueur wines: rancio, white and black mistela, Garnacha, vino dulce natural and Vimblanc.

climate.text: Mediterranean with some continentality: cold winters, hot dry summers, 500 to 600 mm of rain, mostly spring and autumn; strong day-night contrast.

soil.text: Three kinds: calcareous sedimentary soils, granitic sands (Falset) and slate «llicorella» that adds minerality.

tastes.text: Reds: violet-red to brown; fresh or ripe fruit, dairy, floral, spice, balsamic. Whites: greenish to coppery yellow; fresh or ripe fruit, floral.

styles.name: Rancio
styles.text: Oxidative ageing in wood or sun-and-night; spice, nuts, toast, honey; complex, more or less sweet.

styles.name: Mistela
styles.text: White: pale yellow to amber, floral, nutty. Black: orange to red-violet, fruity, honey. Sweet.

styles.name: Garnacha
styles.text: Garnacha grapes, fortified; orange to ruby; floral, fruity, honey, nuts; sweet, balanced.

styles.name: Vimblanc
styles.text: From authorised grapes without skin maceration; orange to ruby; floral, fruity, honey, nuts; sweet, balanced.

why.text: Calcareous soils give the wines a salty note and a long finish. Garnacha Blanca has a long tradition here.

styles.text: Whites (including single-variety Garnacha Blanca), rosados and reds; also sparkling, needle and liqueur wines.

climate.text: Mediterranean and southern in character, with harvests rich in sugar.

tastes.text: Whites: yellow with grey to gold hints; complex, rich aromas; salty on the palate.

styles.name: Rancio
styles.text: Oxidative ageing in sun and night; at least a year in oak.

styles.name: Mistela
styles.text: Spirit added to must of white or black grapes; at least 140 g/l of sugar.

styles.name: Garnacha
styles.text: Liqueur wine from overripe grapes.
